deck.title: Warm & Fuzzies — SUEDE Designathon 2026 pitch draft
deck.narrative_rule: Move from unprompted appreciation to the occasion rule, the evidence gap, the persona moment, one explicit design brief, one solution reveal, one live demo and one team-authored handoff.
deck.evidence_rule: Every plotted matrix position is a team hypothesis. Published studies may support a channel mechanism only when the exact finding and boundary are visible. Survey examples in the transcript are not results. Missing What, Why and How evidence remains visibly blank until documented research exists.

design.direction: Warm & Fuzzies paper-and-ink presentation system derived from Cecelia's current brand board
design.signature: An unprompted-appreciation question becomes an occasion rule, a visibly unproven format gap, an evidence-to-solution deduction, one live giving ritual and a real thank-you object for the room.

slides.audience_takeaway: Meet the product identity and team, then move immediately.

visual.composition: Cecelia's firefly and the Warm & Fuzzies wordmark on white, with the approved team name, team number and confirmed member names. Do not add narrative copy.

speaker_notes: Timing: 5 seconds.
Name the team and move.
Blocked until team number and member-name spelling are confirmed.

motion.description: Reveal the human-drawn identity once; no ambient loop.

slides.claim: When was the last time someone showed you appreciation or gratitude?
slides.audience_takeaway: Recall an unprompted act of appreciation before the team names the problem.

visual.composition: One full-frame question ending with `appreciation or gratitude?` Do not put the birthday or event clarification on the slide. Do not mention letters, because that reveals a solution format before the problem is established. No counterpoint, supporting sentence or raise-hands prompt.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Ask the visible appreciation-or-gratitude question and pause briefly. Then say aloud that birthdays and events do not count.
Do not mention letters, ask for raised hands or add the removed `we have never had more ways to talk` counterpoint.
Audience reflection opens the story; it is not evidence.

motion.description: One question appears once; no staged subtext.

slides.claim: We appreciate our friends and family. We just do not always show it.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the problem as an expression barrier, not missing care.

visual.composition: One plain problem statement in the established navy-and-white colour system. No Chloe attribution, mentor quote, persona, explanatory paragraph or orange detour.

speaker_notes: Timing: 15 seconds.
Say that appreciation can already exist while expressing it on an ordinary day still feels out of the ordinary.
Treat this as the team's current problem framing, not a prevalence finding.

motion.description: Emphasise `show it` only after the full statement lands.

slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the working unwritten rule and the design question it creates.

visual.composition: Birthdays, farewells and milestones each visibly supply permission; an ordinary Tuesday supplies no prompt and an unexpected appreciation text can trigger `Is everything okay?`. Close with one line: `How might we create that permission on an ordinary day?`

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.

Ask why showing appreciation appears to require a socially recognised time. Use the ordinary-Tuesday example: through conventional messaging, an unexpected appreciation message can feel worrying because it sits outside the norm.
The rule and reaction are working hypotheses; their prevalence, boundaries and exceptions still require primary research.

motion.description: Show occasion prompts, then the unprompted ordinary day, then the How Might We.

slides.claim: The possible gap: meaningful enough to matter, low-friction enough to send today.
slides.audience_takeaway: See what published research establishes about each channel, then distinguish those findings from the team's plotted opportunity hypothesis.

visual.composition: A working channel map with `meaning + effort` increasing left-to-right and `cost: time + money + distance` increasing bottom-to-top. Reveal each point with one adjacent-study finding and its boundary: text can carry gratitude but lacks vocal tone; voice can create more connection than text; video did not reliably outperform audio; gratitude letters were less awkward and more positive than senders expected; gift effort predicted gratitude through thoughtfulness while price did not predict appreciation. Remove the unsupported fourth percentage. Finish on an `authored + revisitable` zone labelled as a hypothesis requiring a matched-format receiver test.

speaker_notes: Timing: 60 seconds; this is the longest evidence slide.
Walk left to right and explain the exact displayed finding for each channel. Do not convert adjacent research into a universal channel ranking.
The chart coordinates, axes and highlighted opportunity are the team's synthesis. Published research makes individual mechanisms plausible but does not validate the gap or Warm & Fuzzies.
The matched-format test must compare the same appreciation across text, voice or video, a physical note or gift and the prototype before the plotted opportunity can become a result.

motion.description: Reveal each channel together with its temporary evidence panel, then replace the panel with the bounded product hypothesis.

slides.audience_takeaway: Read the actual What, Why and How findings at presentation distance without relying on explanatory subtext.

visual.composition: Three high-contrast result columns with no headline, footer, source line, bridge or small explanatory copy. `WHAT` pairs the question with a very large `___%` and makes `feel they do not fully show the appreciation they feel` main text. `WHY` reserves a large qualitative answer line rather than pre-filling a theme. `HOW` reserves a large winning-format line tied to impact, effort and frequency. Every blank remains visibly unfilled until documented research exists.

speaker_notes: Timing: 40 seconds.
Move through What, Why and How in order. Read the finding itself, not the research plan around it.

The latest research follow-up confirms these three questions are the complete primary-research instrument for the live story. The visible blanks remain blocked until recruitment, sample, wording, method, analysis, exact results, exceptions and limitations are recorded.

Psychology on text meaningfulness, ownership and the relationship between visible effort and appreciation may support the channel-map mechanism and appendix, but it cannot fill these primary-result blanks.
The transcript's suggested 40, 100, 70 percent, 75 percent, 95 percent and all other example values are brainstorming, not data.
No small-print bridge, method caption or source footer belongs on this live slide.

motion.description: Reveal What, Why and How in order while keeping every pending label visible.

slides.claim: Imagine a grandmother thinking of her granddaughter on an ordinary day.
slides.audience_takeaway: See the moment of use through the grandmother-granddaughter persona relationship the team chose.

visual.composition: Use the grandmother and granddaughter as the visual answer to `when`. Show that they live apart in different time zones, there is no occasion, and a call requires both people to be free. Resolve the scene with grandmother making it now and granddaughter opening it later. Keep the treatment illustrative and avoid invented demographic details or market claims.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.

Use the grandmother-granddaughter relationship to explain when the experience belongs: an ordinary thought, no occasion, physical distance, different time zones and no need for both people to be free.
This remains an illustrative scenario, not validated demand or a research-derived persona. Do not invent demographic details or participant testimony.

motion.description: Move through the ordinary-day trigger, channel tension, finite gesture and receiver-controlled opening.

slides.claim: If people feel they do not fully show appreciation, and the barrier is that it feels out of place, then showing appreciation must feel normal on an ordinary day.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the evidence-led deduction that connects the research results to the solution direction.

visual.composition: A three-step, high-contrast If / And / Then chain. `IF · ___%` feel they do not fully show the appreciation they feel. `AND · ___%` say the barrier is that it feels out of place. `THEN` make showing appreciation feel normal on an ordinary day. Keep both percentages blank until the research supports them.

speaker_notes: Timing: 15 seconds.

Connect the findings before naming the product: if the expression gap exists and participants identify ordinary-day discomfort as the barrier, the design problem becomes normalising appreciation in everyday life.
The second percentage and named barrier must come from coded participant responses. Until then, this remains the intended deduction structure, not a proven need or causal result.

motion.description: Reveal the What result, then the Why result, then the everyday-normalisation requirement that leads into the solution.

slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the proposed ordinary-day ritual in one sentence before the live demonstration.

visual.composition: Product identity, current Home state and one mechanism line only: `Make one appreciation object. Send a link. Let them open it on their own terms.` No process strip, feature inventory, future context layer, anti-doomscroll concept or impact claim.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Introduce the product and switch immediately to the running prototype.
Receiving by link and without another account is the intended low-friction prototype path; production identity and delivery remain unresolved.
Call normalising appreciation a goal, not a proven outcome.

motion.description: Reveal the product name and one mechanism line, then stop deck motion for the live demo.

slides.audience_takeaway: Watch one complete working sender-to-receiver journey rather than a narrated feature tour.

visual.composition: A dark holding slide containing only `Let us show you.` Then leave the deck and begin the live prototype. No process verbs, instruction line, screenshot sequence or video.

speaker_notes: Timing: 100 seconds.
Switch to the live prototype. Show only the critical path: compose one object, seal it, choose its travel, create the link, open as receiver, then keep, close or remove without replying.

Explain the relevant process decision while it appears: why the object shows effort, why sealing creates closure, why the link reduces receiving friction and why the receiver controls the ending. Keep the emphasis on the research logic, not a separate process diary.
Demonstrate only working states. Do not claim delivery infrastructure, verified identity, encrypted privacy, ownership, permanent storage or lower awkwardness.
Use a preloaded static or local fallback only if the live path fails; never spend pitch time showing both a video and the live demo.

motion.description: Deck motion stops while the presenter demonstrates the working prototype; return only after the receiver outcome is visible.

slides.claim: We made something for you, too.
slides.audience_takeaway: Receive a real team-authored thank-you through the same flow, voluntarily and without reply pressure.

visual.composition: The final handoff uses a real approved photo or selfie of the team making the object, a real thank-you object with contributions from the team, and the verified live QR and URL. Include an equally clear no-device fallback. Do not ship a generic placeholder card as the final state.

speaker_notes: Timing: 35 seconds.
Thank the hosts and room, say the team made this object for them, and invite them to open it privately and optionally. No reply is expected.
Blocked until the real team photo has consent, the team-authored object is complete, the deployed receiver URL is tested on a second device, and the QR is verified at presentation distance.
A scan, smile, applause or emotional reaction demonstrates the handoff only; it is not impact evidence.

motion.description: Reveal the real team photo, then the verified handoff card. No separate conclusion slide follows.
